questions.skill: Construct a copy of an angle
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs. Construct an angle with vertex P and one side ray PR that is congruent to ∠ABC.
questions.prompt_markup:
Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs.
Construct an angle with vertex P and one side ray PR that is congruent to ∠ABC.
questions.correct_answer: Arc centered at B meets the sides at D and E; same arc centered at P meets ray PR at F; arc centered at F with radius DE meets the first arc at G; ray PG.
questions.grading_note: Grade the construction marks, not only the final figure: the arc at B, the same-radius arc at P, the arc with radius DE centered on ray PR, and ray PG drawn. The copy may open above or below ray PR.

questions.prompt: Write the steps to copy ∠ABC so that its vertex is at P and one side is ray PR.
questions.prompt_markup: Write the steps to copy ∠ABC so that its vertex is at P and one side is ray PR.
questions.correct_answer: 1. Arc centered at B crossing BA at D and BC at E. 2. Same arc centered at P crossing ray PR at F. 3. Set the compass to DE. 4. Arc centered at F crossing the second arc at G. 5. Draw ray PG.

questions.prompt: Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs. Construct an angle at P on ray PR whose measure is twice m∠ABC.
questions.prompt_markup:
Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs.
Construct an angle at P on ray PR whose measure is twice m∠ABC.
questions.correct_answer: Copy ∠ABC onto ray PR to get ray PG, then copy ∠ABC again onto ray PG (on the other side from R) to get ray PH; ∠RPH = 2∠ABC.
questions.grading_note: Grade the construction marks, not only the final figure: two complete angle copies sharing ray PG.

questions.skill: Justify why the angle-copy construction works
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In copying ∠ABC to ∠FPG, BD = BE = PF = PG (same arc radius) and DE = FG (same compass setting). Prove that ∠DBE ≅ ∠FPG.
questions.prompt_markup: In copying ∠ABC to ∠FPG, BD = BE = PF = PG (same arc radius) and DE = FG (same compass setting). Prove that ∠DBE ≅ ∠FPG.
questions.required_method: Prove △DBE ≅ △FPG by SSS, then use corresponding angles.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: BD = PF, BE = PG, DE = FG (construction); SSS; corresponding angles ∠DBE and ∠FPG.

questions.skill: Use angle copying to construct a parallel line
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs. Construct the line through P parallel to line ℓ by copying an angle.
questions.prompt_markup:
Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs.
Construct the line through P parallel to line ℓ by copying an angle.
questions.correct_answer: Copy the angle that line AP makes with ℓ at A to vertex P, in the corresponding position; the new side through P is parallel to ℓ.
questions.grading_note: Grade the construction marks, not only the final figure: a complete angle copy at P (equal-radius arcs and chord) in the corresponding position, and the line drawn through P.
